crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_1: Wind is everywhere in the world.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_2: Wind is represented in terms of chunks; in addition to the random seed, it is influenced by multiple factors such as air pressure and terrain.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_3: To make sense of the wind, we can use meteorological instruments.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_4: The wind vane reports direction: its arrow points into the wind - the direction it comes from.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_5: The anemometer reports speed. Its cups turn with the wind they catch.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_6: Note that an anemometer made of andesite alloy cannot withstand strong wind.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_7: It gradually turns red to show the load it is under.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_8: When the wind gets too strong - Peng - it is wrecked by the gale.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_9: It is not an instrument suited to windy places such as high mountains.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_10: The weather station reports five things: direction, per-second wind, exact speed, temperature and precipitation.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_11: It is rated for far stronger wind, so it can be used safely in windy places without being destroyed.
crosswind.ponder.instruments.text_12: It has no drawbacks - apart from the price.
crosswind.ponder.tag.instruments.descrip: Instruments that read the local wind field
item.crosswind.non_slip_boots.tooltip: Increases friction while worn: wind-driven sliding is cut to about a quarter (on ground only)
